source.title: Sycophancy Suppression Can Impair Rational Updating: Anti-Sycophancy Should Preserve the Ability to Update
source.authors: Huanhuan Ma; Henry Peng Zou; Cheng-Ze Li; En-Ze Ma; Yunan Su; Philip S. Yu

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures overlap between neuron sets associated with two answer-revision behaviors, but does not test whether individual neurons respond to unrelated input classes or have coherent versus mixed meanings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports MLP-neuron-set overlap, but its top-k sets are selected for attribution to unsupported-yielding and rational-updating; overlap between those sets does not establish that an individual neuron responds to several unrelated inputs. These measurements are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version, not as tests of V1–V7. Behavioral intervention results and steering-direction results do not measure the polysemanticity claim.
record.test_reason: The paper studies sycophancy (unsupported-yielding vs rational-updating) and localizes components by attribution patching. Its MLP-neuron overlap tables measure whether two attribution-selected neuron sets intersect, not whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs, how common such neurons are, or what causes them. It neither tests nor uses polysemanticity as a tool. The only nearby text is a limitations remark that sparse-feature circuit methods (Marks et al., 2025) might separate the behaviors more cleanly. That is closer to citing than to discussing the claim, so the relation is cites_only rather than the reader's discusses; T6 is right.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct and needs one addition. The authors add that orthogonalized steering gives modest, backbone-dependent selectivity gains on TruthfulQA.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not reproduce or apply the original neuron-polysemanticity methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported neuron-set overlap varies with backbone, dataset, and top-k threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-k attribution-selected MLP neuron sets for unsupported-yielding and rational-updating overlap 38–90% at k=50 and 26–80% at k=5000. The random baseline is below 0.03% at k=50 and 1–2% at k=5000. Overlap falls as k grows (Table 10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Components causally attributed to distinct but related behaviors (yielding to pressure vs updating on evidence) overlap far above chance, consistent with a shared substrate rather than with per-neuron polysemanticity.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The analysis uses four open-weight instruction-tuned models and top-k component attribution; the authors note that finer-grained sparse-feature methods might separate the behaviors more clearly. The overlap measurements do not test individual neurons' responses to unrelated input classes. The overlap tables do not report uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No additional neuron-set-overlap values were left out. Other mechanistic results, including steering-direction cosine and cross-patch recovery, are not included because they do not measure individual-neuron polysemanticity or the overlap of the two neuron sets.

untested.parts: Not tested: how many LM MLP neurons respond to unrelated tokens or contexts, and how this varies by layer. Fig 4 layer distributions concern attributed neurons, not polysemantic ones.
Superposition as the cause is not tested.
Polysemanticity without capacity pressure is not tested.
Effects of architecture, activation function or regularization on the share of polysemantic neurons are not tested.
Whether apparent polysemanticity reflects one shared feature is not tested. The overlap could reflect a shared 'answer revision' function, but the paper does not analyze individual neurons.
Dependence on the measurement (activation range examined, explanation scoring) is not tested. Overlap varying with k is a set-selection threshold, not a polysemanticity criterion.

record.verdict_notes: This is a sycophancy paper and is off-topic for polysemantic neurons. Two caveats for the overlap rows. First, the mechanistic analyses on TruthfulQA used an earlier set of LLM-generated evidence notes. Second, the overlap tables give no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: Whether vision-model neurons respond to several unrelated image inputs.
Whether transformer language-model MLP neurons respond to unrelated tokens or contexts, and how common this is across layers.
Whether polysemanticity is caused by sparse features being packed under capacity pressure.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure from initialization, regularization, or training noise.
Whether activation, architecture, or regularization changes polysemantic-neuron prevalence or permits reducing it without substantial performance loss.
Whether apparently polysemantic neurons instead detect a shared feature or related jobs, and how common truly unrelated mixtures are.
Whether polysemanticity judgments depend on the activation range examined or the explanation-scoring method.

relation.reason: The text never mentions polysemanticity or superposition and cites none of its sources. The nearest nod is a limitations remark that sparse-feature circuits (Marks et al., 2025) might separate the two behaviours more cleanly. cites_only is the weakest relation available and fits best; tests, uses, assumes and discusses do not apply.

tranche.reason: Studies sycophancy and measures overlap between neuron sets selected by attribution for two behaviours. It never tests whether single neurons respond to unrelated inputs, so it neither tests nor uses the claim.

source_check.notes: All 20 sampled rows match Tables 8 and 10. Table 8 is laid out with models as columns and datasets as rows, values given as k=50 / k=5000 (%). The values are overlaps between neuron sets selected by attribution for each behaviour, not measures of polysemanticity, so cannot_determine and no linked versions are right. The paper does not cite any polysemanticity source, and it has no verdicts. The evidence-writing prompt in the appendix is quoted and is not an instruction to readers.
